spec_match.rationale: Every page calls Iterator.prototype.join when it exists and otherwise runs a shim written from the proposal's own steps, labelled as a shim on the page itself. separator-semantics derives the contract by running the platform's Array.prototype.join side by side rather than restating rules from memory — which is what caught the shim using String() (returns "Symbol(s)") where the spec's ToString throws.

interactive.rationale: Four working surfaces: a pipeline runner with live source/take/separator controls and a pull counter, a separator matrix driven by a select plus free text, a log formatter that filters and reshapes pasted input, and a timed comparison at a chosen size.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index frames the feature as the missing terminal operation on the lazy helper pipeline — the proposal's own motivation — and each card describes what its page actually does.

edge_cases.rationale: null/undefined elements, an omitted versus explicitly-undefined separator, non-string separators coerced with ToString, nested arrays, the empty sequence, and the symbol case that must throw. The formatter also covers the filter-matches-nothing branch.

references.rationale: chromestatus.com/feature/5095183554314240 on the index and on all four concept pages, alongside the TC39 proposal and the ECMA-262 Array.prototype.join section.

conformance.rationale: Seven immutable assertions: %Iterator.prototype% identity, helper presence as the precondition, the method's existence and arity, full parity against Array.prototype.join over six inputs and five separators, the nullish-to-empty-string reference rule, and the ToString/symbol TypeError.

runtime_evidence.rationale: deno task drive over all four pages in real Chrome 150, twice: with V8 staging off (4/4, 28 assertions, shim path) and with --js-flags=--harmony on (4/4, 28 assertions, native path). Under the native method the separator matrix agrees with Array.prototype.join on all eight cases across six separators, so the parity claim is a measurement of the engine and not only of this page's shim. Laziness is proved by measured pull counts (6 pulled from a source of 1000; 11 pulled to yield 6 odd numbers), not asserted.

telemetry_health.rationale: Each page emits showcaseTelemetry.assert with the numbers it just measured (pull counts, agreement counts, output lengths, native-vs-shim).

design_system.rationale: CSS variables throughout, no raw colour literals, every local button rule sets background and colour, 44px control minimums, tables and pre blocks scroll inside their own containers.

accessibility.rationale: Labelled controls, a fieldset/legend for the level checkboxes, semantic tables with scope and caption, aria-live output for every recomputed result, focusable pre blocks for the scrollable code and result panes.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Control grids are auto-fit minmax with align-content:start so they collapse to one column without stretching; long output uses overflow-wrap:anywhere and per-container overflow-x. Recorded via responsive-check on both classes.

openQuestions.title: Re-run the parity matrix once Chrome ships the native method
openQuestions.detail: Every page currently exercises the shim path in stable Chrome. When Iterator.prototype.join lands, the separator-semantics table becomes a genuine implementation check rather than a check of this page's own shim, and the array-vs-accumulate timing row becomes engine-versus-engine instead of engine-versus-JavaScript. Nothing needs changing to make that happen — but the copy that explains the shim should be re-read against what the page then shows.

guidanceConsulted.query: live region for results updated by a button
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Announce recomputed results through a live region rather than relying on visual change, and keep every control labelled and keyboard-operable.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Each page routes its narrative result through an aria-live output element that is rewritten on every recompute; all inputs are wrapped in labels with for/id, and the level filters use fieldset/legend.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: deno task drive exercises every control by keyboard-equivalent events; each case asserts the detail text was written.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive data table without horizontal overflow
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use intrinsic sizing and auto-fit grids for control panels, and give wide content its own scroll container instead of letting the page scroll sideways.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Control rows are grid auto-fit minmax(170–200px) with align-content:start; tables and result panes carry overflow-x/overflow-wrap so the body never scrolls horizontally at 360px.

summary: Four concepts covering the basic call, the exact separator/element contract, a practical formatter, and the cost argument the proposal rests on. The build found and fixed one real error in its own shim (String() versus ToString on symbols), which the separator matrix surfaced precisely because it compares against the platform rather than against my description of it.
